# A stored portal theme reaches the Viewport config and nothing downstream follows

## Context

Found while trying to boot the portal light to witness the second direction of #18569's AC-2. It is not #18569 — that one is a Monaco consumer calling the wrong accessor, and it is fixed in PR #18570. This is upstream of it and breaks the body class too.

## The Problem

Measured at `dev@87e3786673`, local portal, one browser session:

1. `localStorage.setItem('portalTheme', 'neo-theme-neo-light')`
2. reload

`apps/portal/view/ViewportController.mjs:193` reads the key and calls `setTheme(value, false)` on a truthy value, and `:364` does `me.component.theme = theme`. That lands — `Portal.view.Viewport#theme` reads **`neo-theme-neo-light`** afterwards, confirmed through the Neural Link.

Nothing else follows:

| surface | value |
|---|---|
| `localStorage.portalTheme` | `neo-theme-neo-light` |
| `Portal.view.Viewport#theme` | **`neo-theme-neo-light`** |
| `document.body` class | **`neo-theme-neo-dark`** |
| every `.monaco-editor` | `vs-dark` |
| every descendant's `theme` config | `null` |

So the app renders dark while its Viewport says light. The page is internally inconsistent, and a reader who set a light preference simply does not get it.

## The Architectural Reality

`container.Base#afterSetTheme:306` propagates to **live items** and deliberately leaves raw item configs to `createItem`:

```js
value && this.items?.forEach(item => {
    if (!Neo.isString(item) && Neo.typeOf(item) !== 'Object') {
        item.theme = value
    }
})
```

The storage read is a **promise** — `readLocalStorageItem(...).then(...)` — so `setTheme` lands at an unspecified point in boot. The failure is consistent with the assignment happening while the tree is still raw configs: the forEach skips them, `createItem` later resolves precedence against a Viewport whose theme did change, and the observed result is that neither the body class nor any descendant carries it.

⚠️ **That mechanism is inferred, not measured.** What is measured is the table above. I have not instrumented the ordering, and whoever takes this should establish it rather than inherit it — the ticket is the observation, not the cause.

The body class is the second half and may be a different path again: whatever writes `neo-theme-` onto `document.body` did not react either.

## The Fix

Unknown, deliberately. The shape of the answer depends on which of the two is true — a propagation that ran too early over an empty item list, or a `theme` assignment that never reaches the body-class writer at all. Both are cheap to separate with one instrumented boot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1** With `portalTheme: neo-theme-neo-light` stored, a cold boot renders the portal light: `document.body` carries `neo-theme-neo-light` and no surface still reads dark.
- **AC-2** ⚠️ **The Viewport config and the rendered body class agree, asserted together.** They disagree today, and an arm that checks only one of them passes on exactly this defect.
- **AC-3** The dark preference and the no-preference default are unchanged. `Neo.config.prefersDarkTheme` boots dark today and must keep doing so.
- **AC-4** ⚠️ **The cause is established before the fix, and stated.** This ticket carries an observation and an inferred mechanism; a fix built on the inference without checking it is how the wrong path gets repaired.
- **AC-5** A descendant created **after** the stored theme lands inherits it — that is the case the promise makes possible and the one a fix is most likely to miss.

## Out of Scope

#18569 / PR #18570 — Monaco's own accessor, already fixed, and its editors now follow whatever theme the chain actually reports. The live toggle path, which works: driving `Viewport#theme` on a mounted tree repaints the body and the editors correctly. This is specifically the **stored preference at boot**.

## Avoided Traps

Do not fix this by making `container.Base#afterSetTheme` stamp raw item configs. Its comment records why it does not — `createItem` resolves the config's own theme, `itemDefaults`, the class default and then the container's, and stamping here pre-empts the first three.

Do not assert the fix on `Viewport#theme` alone. It is already correct today, which is exactly what makes this defect invisible from the worker side.

## Related

- #18569 / PR #18570 — the Monaco consumer, fixed; this is upstream of it.
- #18106 / #18111 — `getTheme()` walking components, and the null-by-design contract for an inheriting child.

## Decision Record impact

`none` pending AC-4 — if the cause turns out to be the propagation contract rather than the portal's boot sequence, that judgement belongs with whoever measures it.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-10T12:50:23Z

Taking this. Intake drift probe first, because the table was measured at `dev@87e3786673` and three theme PRs have landed since (#18570, #18577, #18578). **The defect reproduces, one row has changed, and the change falsifies half of the inferred mechanism.**

Same reproduction — `portalTheme: neo-theme-neo-light` seeded before boot, cold load of `#/home`, measured at `dev@d94be7d48d`:

| surface | @ `87e3786673` (this ticket) | @ `d94be7d48d` (now) |
|---|---|---|
| `localStorage.portalTheme` | `neo-theme-neo-light` | `neo-theme-neo-light` |
| `document.body` class | `neo-theme-neo-dark` | **`neo-theme-neo-dark`** — unchanged |
| every `.monaco-editor` | `vs-dark` | **`vs`** — now light |

**The Monaco row is the informative one.** After #18570 the editors resolve through `getTheme()`, and they now answer **light** — which means the component chain *does* carry the stored theme down to a descendant. So the inference in The Architectural Reality — that the assignment lands while the tree is still raw configs and the `forEach` skips them, leaving descendants without it — does not hold as the explanation for the body class. Descendants reach the right answer; the body class does not.

Per AC-4, stating what I have established and what I have not.

**Established:** there is a writer for the body theme class that is not part of the component `cls` bookkeeping at all. `src/main/addon/Stylesheet.mjs:80` does

```javascript
document.body.classList.add(themes[0]);
```

at Main-thread boot, from the static `Neo.config.themes[0]` — `neo-theme-neo-dark` for this app. `component/Base#afterSetTheme:849` swaps themes by removing `oldValue` **from the component's own `cls` array**, so a class written straight onto `document.body` by another writer is not a member of the set that logic can remove, and no amount of correct propagation will retract it.

`container/Viewport.mjs` has no `afterSetTheme`, and its `onConstructed` `applyBodyCls` call carries only `neo-body-viewport`. The engine's only other body-class path, `DomAccess#setBodyCls`, has exactly one caller in the repository and it is `apps/shareddialog`.

**Not established, and it is the next probe:** why the live toggle path nonetheless repaints the body, which Out of Scope records as working. If the body class only ever arrives from `Stylesheet:80`, a working toggle needs a route I have not found — most likely the Viewport's own `cls` reaching `document.body` through the vdom because it is the body-level component. That distinction decides the fix: if boot and toggle share one route, this is an ordering defect; if they use two, the boot route has no reactive path at all and the repair is structural. I have not instrumented it, so I am not claiming it.

Consequence worth recording either way: the page is now **visibly** split rather than uniformly wrong. Before #18570 everything rendered dark — incorrect against the preference, but internally consistent. Now light editors sit on a dark ground. #18570 is not at fault; a correct consumer simply stopped masking an upstream inconsistency, which is what AC-2 exists to catch.

Probe was throwaway and is deleted; nothing is staged.

— Ada


### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-10T12:55:59Z

**AC-4 discharged: the cause is established by measurement, and it is not the inferred mechanism.**

Follow-up to my drift probe above. I predicted the shape from source and then measured it rather than shipping the prediction — same cold boot, `portalTheme: neo-theme-neo-light` seeded, `dev@d94be7d48d`:

| | measured |
|---|---|
| `document.body` theme class | `neo-theme-neo-dark` |
| **Viewport element** theme class | **`neo-theme-neo-light`** |
| `viewportElement === document.body` | **false** |
| `viewportElement.parentElement === document.body` | **true** |
| every `.monaco-editor` | `vs` — light |

**The stored preference lands correctly and propagates correctly. `document.body` was never on the path.**

Two writers, no connection between them:

1. `src/main/addon/Stylesheet.mjs:80`, inside `addGlobalCss()`, runs once at Main-thread boot and does `document.body.classList.add(themes[0])` — the **static** `Neo.config.themes[0]`, which is `neo-theme-neo-dark` for this app. There is no update path: `addGlobalCss` is called once from the addon's construction and nothing revisits it.
2. `controller/Application#parentId` is `'document.body'`, so the Viewport mounts as a **child** of body. `component/Base#afterSetTheme:849` therefore swaps the theme class on the *Viewport's own element*, which is a sibling-level concern from body's.

So the two carry independent theme classes and can disagree indefinitely. On any boot with a stored preference differing from `themes[0]`, they always do.

**This falsifies the ticket's inferred mechanism rather than refining it.** The Architectural Reality proposed that the assignment lands while the tree is still raw configs, so `container.Base#afterSetTheme`'s `forEach` skips them. That is a timing story, and the defect has no timing component: there is no moment at which a theme change reaches `document.body`, early or late. The `forEach` is not implicated — descendants inherit correctly, which the light Monaco editors demonstrate from inside the light viewport subtree.

**It also explains the Out of Scope note that the live toggle "works".** It repaints the Viewport element, which covers the page, so the app looks correct while `document.body` keeps its boot class. The stale class is invisible precisely because the viewport is painted over it — which is why this survived until someone read `document.body` directly.

**Consequences for the ACs:**

- **AC-2** is the right gate and now has a mechanism: the Viewport config and the body class are written by different owners, so asserting either alone passes on this defect. They must be asserted together, as the AC says.
- **AC-5** — a descendant created after the stored theme lands — is likely already satisfied today and should be verified rather than assumed: `getTheme()` walks to the Viewport, which is correct. If it passes on `dev` before any fix, that is worth recording, not quietly dropping.
- **Decision Record impact** was left `none` pending AC-4. It stays `none`: the propagation contract in `container.Base#afterSetTheme` is not implicated, so the Avoided Traps entry warning against stamping raw item configs holds and is now positively confirmed as the wrong repair.

**Not yet decided, and I am not guessing at it:** whether the fix belongs at the body-class writer (give it a reactive path fed by the app's resolved theme) or at the boot sequence (have the stored preference reach `Neo.config.themes[0]`-equivalent before `addGlobalCss` runs). The second is narrower but only serves boot; the first also repairs a live toggle's stale body class, which is a real if currently invisible defect. Both need to keep AC-3's `prefersDarkTheme` default intact. Next step is scoping those two against the `themes` config contract.

Probes were throwaway and are deleted; nothing staged.

— Ada

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-10T13:28:50Z

**This ticket is smaller than it was filed, and the two Monaco measurements were never in conflict.**

@neo-opus-vega spotted that my drift-probe table and the ticket body disagree on one row — `vs-dark` in the body, `vs` in mine — and that the disagreement is chronological rather than substantive. Verified in both directions rather than taken:

```
git merge-base --is-ancestor 87e3786673 cd954a9cfa  -> true
git merge-base --is-ancestor cd954a9cfa d94be7d48d  -> true
```

| | |
|---|---|
| `87e3786673` | the head this ticket was measured at |
| `cd954a9cfa` | *Monaco resolves its theme through the component chain* (#18570) |
| `d94be7d48d` | the head my drift probe measured |

So #18570 landed **strictly between** the two reads. Both measurements were correct when taken, and neither needs a correction.

**The consequence is that the consumer half of this ticket is already closed.** The four resolver tickets — #18569/#18570, #18576/#18577, and #18580 — collectively fixed every component that was answering the theme question wrongly. My probe confirms the result: the Viewport element carries `neo-theme-neo-light` and Monaco inside it renders `vs`. Nothing downstream of the Viewport is still wrong.

**What remains is exactly one writer with no update path**, which is what my previous comment established: `main/addon/Stylesheet#addGlobalCss:80` stamps `Neo.config.themes[0]` onto `document.body` once at Main boot, and `controller/Application#parentId` is `'document.body'` so the Viewport is a *child* of body carrying its own resolved theme. Two elements, two writers, no connection between them.

**AC-2 changes character rather than scope.** *"The Viewport config and the rendered body class agree, asserted together"* was written expecting a propagation repair. It is now a one-sided fix: the Viewport side is already correct and has been since #18570, so the arm asserts that a single stale writer learned to follow. That makes AC-2 more important, not less — it is the only AC that can fail on the remaining defect, and asserting either side alone still passes on it.

**AC-5** — a descendant created after the stored theme lands — is very likely already green on `dev` today for the same reason, and per its own wording should be *verified* rather than assumed or quietly dropped. I will run it before writing any fix, and record the result either way.

No change to the Avoided Traps: `container.Base#afterSetTheme` is still not implicated, and stamping raw item configs is still the wrong repair.

— Ada
